substantive_findings.source_label: sec:intro / paragraph “Backward attribution, however, is usually presented as a zoo of recipes”
substantive_findings.missing_substance: The Ancona et al. comparison and citation have been restored verbatim with an added bridge to the split framework.

Paper statement specifies AI use for baseline/evaluation implementation, plots/tables, text drafting/editing; disclaims AI generation of research ideas, game formulation, theorems and proofs; states author review/testing and responsibility. The thesis declaration requires disclosure but does not preserve these specific facts. Given the thesis also includes Lean proof work, the original paper assertion cannot be presented as a current thesis-wide disclosure without attribution/context.
substantive_findings.recommended_placement: Retain only as a clearly attributed statement about the original paper in the appendix, as root plans; do not use it as the thesis-wide AI disclosure.

substantive_findings.missing_substance: No substantive gap remains. The three-paragraph cautionary discussion is present; terminology is lightly adapted.
substantive_findings.recommended_placement: Add a brief broader-impact paragraph to tex/chapters/09_conclusion.tex (limitations) or an appendix, retaining the source text as much as appropriate.

substantive_findings.missing_substance: Same image is used, but label is renamed to fig:game_trajectory_overview and caption is condensed; original caption describes the backward pass as a trajectory distribution and likely connects to the changed intro terminology.
substantive_findings.recommended_placement: No asset missing. Consider carrying over explicit “distribution of backward trajectories” language in the caption if preserving source framing.

substantive_findings.missing_substance: Main interpretation, exact-vs-deformed scope, benchmark caveats, trajectory-level diagnostic and future-work caution are represented in the thesis conclusion/limitations. Exact prose is not retained, consistently with thesis-wide synthesis; no separate claim-level omission found beyond the AI statement and broader impact above.

global_checks.citation_identity: All 72 unique source citation keys are now represented in active thesis chapters after applying reports/paper-v2-citation-aliases.json; the Ancona2018 comparison/citation was restored. All 72 cited source references have source bibliography records; all corresponding thesis bibliography records exist in the thesis bibliography source. The current tex/main.bbl contains 143 entries and predates the just-restored Ancona citation (Ancona2018 is not yet emitted in the cached BBL).
global_checks.figures_tables: Existing report reports/paper-v2-integration-audit.md records byte-identical imported counterparts for all 69 referenced figures and all 19 generated tables, with adapted wrapper only for sanity-check table. Main figure asset also reused under a changed label/caption.
global_checks.math_proofs: All labeled source equations/theorems/lemmas/propositions in the core technical appendix have matching thesis labels after stripping the ptnb: namespace; mathematical differences are subject to reports/mathematical-corrections.md and are not counted as omissions.
global_checks.limitations: No builds or edits performed by this audit.

source_to_thesis_label_entries_note: coverage_entries enumerates every source label and nearest source heading. Exact-label matches establish a location but do not alone establish text equivalence; the substantive_findings and global_checks record semantic checks and merge gaps.

verbatim_retention_estimate.method: Heuristic paragraph comparison over source main technical body plus supplement (source lines 335–758 and 783 onward) against active thesis chapters 04, 05, 07, 08, 10, and 11; strip labels/references/citation syntax and common presentation/acronym wrappers, then compare normalized word sequences against the closest thesis paragraph. This is an estimate, not a proof of exact textual identity.
verbatim_retention_estimate.estimate: About 83% of source prose words fall in paragraphs with >=98% normalized sequence similarity; about 97% fall in paragraphs at >=80% similarity; word-weighted best paragraph similarity is about 97%. These figures include changes from thesis restructuring, namespaced labels, citation aliases, and documented mathematical corrections. The separately rewritten source Introduction and Discussion are excluded from this technical-body estimate.
verbatim_retention_estimate.substantive_reading: The technical appendix/proofs, detailed protocol and result narratives are retained at high fidelity. Remaining deliberate or material non-verbatim content is concentrated in the intro/conclusion synthesis and AI statement framing, rather than dropped methods, equations, theorem arguments, experiments or result figures.
